roles.claim_profile: Demo: the deployment test-jurisdiction set (DEC-16 values as reference data: in-scope root, one out-of-scope code, `UNKNOWN`). Pilot: subtrees from access review.
As analyst (must reach every test context to inspect fail-safe outcomes).
Scope roots of the packs the user maintains; `*` only for the internal L0 maintainer (DEC-45).
As policy_author. No user holds the role while DEC-11 is unresolved.
Scope roots of the packs the user activates; `*` only where L0 activation is delegated (DEC-45).

ISLAMIC deployments only (DEC-55): `*` for the institution overlay pack plus the deployment's jurisdiction roots. The issuer creates no user with this role in CONVENTIONAL deployments, and none until DEC-63 records a named person.
Granted by the host integration config; subset of the deployment scope plus `UNKNOWN` if the host sends incomplete context.

jurisdiction_check_classes.rule: Only `ri_deployment` must equal the instance `deployment_id`; governance or operational metadata with no customer data.

Every attribute of the request `jurisdiction_context` (residence, booking entity, servicing location) must lie inside a subtree listed in `ri_jurisdictions`; otherwise 403 `JURISDICTION_NOT_PERMITTED`. Checked before the PDP runs.

The stored item's recorded jurisdiction context (customer, recommendation, retention action, review item, decision `jurisdiction_set`) must lie inside `ri_jurisdictions`; otherwise 403 `JURISDICTION_NOT_PERMITTED`.
List and export results contain only rows whose recorded jurisdiction lies inside `ri_jurisdictions`; governance rows with an empty jurisdiction set are included. No 403.

Batch input rows (consent, preferences, ingest parts) for a customer whose supplied or stored residence lies outside `ri_jurisdictions` are rejected individually with issue `JURISDICTION_NOT_PERMITTED`; other rows proceed.
The target pack `scope_root` (or every overlay control `jurisdiction_scope`) must lie inside `ri_jurisdictions`; a `*` (L0) pack needs `*` in the claim. Otherwise 403 `JURISDICTION_NOT_PERMITTED`.

jurisdiction_conditions.condition: Token `ri_deployment` differs from the instance `deployment_id` (any scope)
REQUEST_CONTEXT scope: a context attribute lies outside `ri_jurisdictions`
STORED_SUBJECT scope: the stored item's jurisdiction lies outside `ri_jurisdictions`
PACK_SCOPE scope: pack `scope_root` or overlay scope lies outside `ri_jurisdictions`
ROW_REJECT scope: batch row for a customer outside `ri_jurisdictions` (row rejected)
ROW_FILTER scope: list/export row outside `ri_jurisdictions` (row omitted)
REQUEST_CONTEXT scope: context inside the claim but outside the deployment scope (or `UNKNOWN`): call allowed, PDP returns the restrictive default (`UNSUPPORTED_JURISDICTION` / DEC-24)
Any held scope: claim and deployment match and context inside the claim and the deployment scope

access_purposes.use_case: Relationship staff open a customer they are serving (S01 -> S02, UJ-1)
Analyst reviews insight or data-quality outcomes for a narrowed set (S01 -> S02)

client_purpose_registry.note: Per machine client (client_id) registrations live in the issuer client registry (reference data ACCESS_PURPOSE_REGISTRY, maker-checker); no client is registered in contract 1.2.0, so every service token is denied

separation_of_duties.rule: maker != approver: no role holds both ri.policy.author and ri.policy.approve; the approval call also checks the user (409 MAKER_CHECKER_VIOLATION)
policy_author cannot approve or activate (no ri.policy.approve, no ri.policy.release)
policy_release cannot author or approve (no ri.policy.author, no ri.policy.approve); activator != maker is checked per user
auditor is read-only: holds no scope marked write
service-only scopes (ri.transactions.enrich, ri.consent.write, ri.ingest.write, ri.ingest.read, ri.dsr.write, ri.policy.overlay.write) are held by no staff role
ri.policy.approve is held only by policy_approver, and the demo issuer creates no policy_approver user while DEC-11 is unresolved
reviewer != requester on review transitions (409 MAKER_CHECKER_VIOLATION); ReviewerRole in outcome schemas is limited to analyst and relationship_staff
nobody, in any role, sees customer names; the name reveal screen does not exist (S12)

Customer directory (contract 1.2.0, DEC-68): only analyst and relationship_staff hold ri.customers.list; auditor and service_host never do; every holder has at least one registered access purpose and every purpose is registered to a holder; listCustomers is deprecated and not implemented

Sharia maker-checker (DEC-55): only sharia_approver holds ri.sharia.approve; sharia_approver holds no ri.policy.author, ri.policy.approve or ri.policy.release; the call also checks Sharia approver != maker per user (409 MAKER_CHECKER_VIOLATION)
